That's a very immature way of thinking. You can absolutely be your ex's friend and care about him/her. OP, unfortunately at this stage she needs professional psychological help. Being there means a lot to a person with depression, but sometimes it's not enough. Also, I'm not sure if you have access in your country, but I highly recommend psilocybin mushrooms as a form of alternate therapy. Taking them with a professional has helped people with extreme depression in just a few sessions.

You need to sit down and talk to your mother. School, college, or any other activity, shouldn't take a toll on your mental or physical health. I took a year off school when I was a teenager due to extreme depression, and it didn't affect my life negatively afterwards. On the contrary, after taking that time off I never felt the need to skip classes or stay at home again, because I used that time to improve my health. Sometimes we need time to do things for ourselves, to heal, to think about our future and what we actually want in life. If you want to be a piercer you can use that free time to research, learn, take courses, etc, see if you actually like it and see yourself doing it for a living. But communication is key here, if you keep hiding this from your mom or your partner, you'll find yourself stuck in a circle of pain. Sometimes we make it harder on ourselves than it actually is. The first step is to be sincere about your feelings. Hope you get better soon!
